title: Village Attacks - Take a look
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zsaXdCEuYsY

Daniel (@dungeondive) unboxes the Village Attacks Kickstarter from Grimlord Games, filmed in his kitchen with the dogs behaving and a warning that a channel update is coming: things will be changing. Village Attacks is a reverse dungeon crawl. It's co-op, but the players are the monsters, defending their castle against waves of villagers and hero-villagers — tower defence in dungeon-crawl clothing. He backed it blind for the art, a folklore-meets-steampunk look he compares to Zombicide: Black Plague, Diablo 3 and, when a log-ram trap card turns up, Bloodborne ("that's probably why I backed this game").

Inside: five playable monsters on thick dashboards with backstories — Banshee, Succubus, Lich, Vampire and the Dullahan, an Irish headless horseman wielding a whip of human spine that he has never heard of; unpunched double-sided tiles with excellent painted lighting; a trap deck of swinging blades, spike pits, chandeliers and crushing walls; hero-villagers like the Gravedigger and Executioner on solid punchboard. The Kickstarter extras add a troll loyal to neither side, 3D trap miniatures, and three monster-and-hero packs drawn from Native American, Slavic (Baba Yaga, Vodyanoy) and Gaelic folklore, plus one exclusive Grim Lord and Revenant.

He grumbles at a single troll shipped in a full-size box, pleads with Kickstarter publishers to pay for professional rulebook editing, and confesses to burnout on games with too much stuff — his Shadows of Brimstone collection fills three tables. Village Attacks, refreshingly, does not.

----

Village Attacks flips the crawl: you are the monsters holding the castle. Which game has best cast you as the dungeon's defender rather than its invader?
